alt_text: Two men in business attire look at a smartphone together in a bright modern meeting room with large windows and a long wooden conference table. in Polanco, Mexico City. Text on the image: What a Business English programme needs
caption:
A good Business English programme is not a generic course with a business cover. Whether you are in Mexico City or anywhere else, it should include four things. First, a proper level test. Starting from a guess means wasted weeks on material that is too easy or too hard. Second, goals tied to real meetings. 'Improve my English' is vague. 'Lead the Monday update without reading from my notes' is something you can train for. Third, practice with your own documents. Your emails, proposals and reports hold the exact language you need. Fourth, progress you can measure. Agree clear markers at the start, then review them at set points. If a programme cannot explain these four, keep asking questions.
